decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up left-arm approach, raising and orienting toward the mallet handle; right arm stays parked.
Move above the left end of the horizontal mallet, gradually yawing the downward grasp to align across its shaft.
Complete shaft alignment while approaching above its left-side grasp point, keeping the left elbow raised.
Lower open fingers around the handle with a small lateral and yaw correction based on the wrist view.
Correct the wrist-view lateral offset and shaft angle before closing; remain at the current approach height.
Fine-align the shaft at the finger center, lower slightly and close the left gripper around the handle.
Allow the fingers to finish closing, then lift gently to check that the mallet travels with the left gripper.
Lift the retained mallet clear and carry its tip toward the first, leftmost red key while keeping the handle in the left workspace.
Center the mallet head along the leftmost red bar and approach its surface gradually; retain the closed grasp.
Make the first downward strike on the red key with small vertical increments; inspect contact before lifting.
Finish the red-key tap, then lift vertically by 5.5 cm before advancing to the orange key.
Advance one key to the right while lifted, then tap the orange key with the mallet head.
Complete the orange-key contact, lift the mallet 5.5 cm, and shift above the yellow key.
Tap the third, yellow key and lift vertically by 5.6 cm before moving to green.
Move above the fourth, green key while clear of the bars, then strike downward and briefly settle.
Lift clear after green, then align over the light-blue key with a slight tip-down tilt to give the fingers more clearance.
Fine-center on the fifth, light-blue key and lower for a controlled tap with the fingers raised by the slight tilt.
Lift 5.5 cm after the light-blue key, then move the mallet above the sixth, dark-blue key.
Replan after the continuity guard: the executed lift already exceeds 2.5 cm. Shift toward dark blue using smaller increments at this height.
Back away slightly from the reach boundary while lowering and centering on dark blue; preserve elbow-up continuity with small initial increments.
Finish the dark-blue tap, lift 3.75 cm, then shift toward the seventh purple key while keeping the left hand on its side.
Center the head on the seventh purple key, strike with a short descent, and begin lifting without moving across other keys.
Complete a lift greater than 2.5 cm after purple, then position above the final magenta key, keeping the left wrist on the left side.
Replan from the executed lift: retract slightly for joint margin while yawing the mallet to preserve tip alignment, then approach the last key laterally.
Strike the final magenta key and lift the mallet vertically by 3.6 cm after contact.
The sequence is not confirmed complete. Return above the left end without touching keys, increasing tip-down angle for clearer mallet-only contacts on a verification pass.
Position over the first red key and lower the tilted mallet toward a clear head-only strike, away from the key-end peg.
Correct the tip from the red key's left edge to its central playing area while lifted, then make a deeper controlled red-key tap.
Finish the centered red tap, lift 4.8 cm vertically, and advance one key to orange.
Use the visible mallet-head position to correct alignment over orange, then descend for the second centered tap.
Lift well clear after orange, shift to the yellow key, and make a centered downward strike while maintaining the closed grasp.
Lift 4.5 cm after yellow, move one key right, and strike the green bar with the mallet head.
Lift more than 2.5 cm after green, advance to light blue, and strike while preserving elbow-up joint continuity.
Lift after light blue with a small retreat for joint margin, then move right and tap dark blue.
After the guard interruption, use small diagonal increments to center and tap dark blue without a large elbow-joint change.
Lift after dark blue, retreat slightly while yawing to keep the tip aligned, then tap the seventh purple key.
Replan from the completed lift using small downward-right increments to reach and strike purple without exceeding the elbow continuity margin.
Lift the mallet head after purple by raising and un-tilting it while retreating for joint margin; extend the tip toward the last key without crossing the left wrist.
Strike the final magenta key with the aligned mallet head, then lift vertically by 4.8 cm after contact.
Raise the mallet substantially farther after the final tap, retreating for elbow margin because the head appeared to settle within the grasp.
Return above the first key with generous clearance and angle the handle forward so the fingers stay in front of the instrument during another controlled sequence.
Align the mallet head with the red bar's middle and descend cautiously with the fingers held in front of the keys.
Correct the head onto the center of the red key and continue the downward tap; the fingers remain in front of the instrument.
Lift a full 10 cm after the red-key contact, allow the mallet to settle in the grasp, then move above orange.
Descend onto the orange key after the full lift, compensating slightly for the head's projected alignment, and allow brief contact.
Lift the mallet 10 cm after the centered orange tap, then advance above the yellow key without touching other bars.
Make the third yellow-key strike from the full raised position, with a small alignment correction and a brief contact dwell.
Lift a full 10 cm after yellow, let the grasp settle, and advance over the fourth green key.
Align from the raised head position and strike the fourth green key, keeping the fingers in front of the instrument.
Lift 10 cm after green, then align over light blue using the observed contact point to avoid drifting to a key edge.
Strike the fifth light-blue key from the full raised position, keeping the mallet aligned and allowing brief contact before the next lift.
Lift the mallet a full 10 cm after light blue, settle the grasp, and advance above the sixth dark-blue key.
Strike the sixth dark-blue key from the fully lifted position, compensating slightly for perspective and briefly settling at contact.
